name: Race Timing style
touchpoints: race broadcasts' timing tower and tyre graphics, the onboard display (shift lights, gear readout, dials), circuit maps with sector and mini-sector colours, speed and delta traces, pit boards and official timing documents

sample.topic: Race debrief of Vizney Racing, a fictional team in a fictional 22-round series: rounds 16 Denver, 17 Seattle and 18 Boston, 20 cars, ours are car 27 (MAR) and car 12 (REY). Times in seconds, points 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1

canvas.role: page background, header and footer (formula1.com results pages put black and #15151e side by side, measured)

card.role: every panel: figures, tables and the workbench sit on #15151e with 8px corners, no border and no shadow (formula1.com results panels, measured); the onboard display is a deeper #0d0d14 face with a 1px #303037 rim and 24px corners

plot.role: chart background: the card itself, never a second panel

raise.role: our rows in the timing tower and the bench, pit-cycle shading in Figure 3, the tooltip (formula1.com raised panel #1c1c25, measured)

sunk.role: the onboard display's face, the circuit's track band, the code window and package panel, the rounds-to-go band, bar tracks in tables

hair.role: row rules and gridlines (formula1.com table rules, 1px #303037, measured)

rule.role: header rules, position-box outlines, axis ticks, the neutral status band (formula1.com #47464c, measured)

ink.role: titles, values, our cars (the subject), the selected round and position boxes, the focus ring

body.role: body text and table values (12.9:1 on the card)

muted.role: axis ticks, notes, subtitles and turn numbers (7.8:1 on the card)

text-2.role: labels, table heads and keys in condensed capitals (formula1.com table heads #aaaaaa, measured)

best.role: purple: fastest of the race, as on timing screens. White text on it 4.9:1

good.role: green: improved, personal best, target or plan met. Text on it #15151e, 6.0:1

missed.role: yellow: target or plan missed, slower than before. Text on it #15151e, 5.9:1

validation.tool: dataviz validate_palette.js (OKLab), mode dark, on the card #15151e where every chart sits, run 2026-11-12
validation.status: purple #8c51d9, green #04a97a, yellow #b88c19 and red #cc3336 pass every check with --pairs all: lightness band 0.48–0.67, chroma ≥ 0.1, worst CVD ΔE 9.7 (yellow↔green, protan; tritan 14.5), worst normal-vision ΔE 17.2, contrast ≥ 3:1. Status always carries a word and ▲/▼ as well
validation.tyres: soft #cc3336 and medium #b88c19: CVD ΔE 10.5 (deutan), normal 19.8. Hard #d9dce2 is the white of the hard compound on purpose, so it sits above the lightness band and below the chroma floor; it separates from soft and medium by lightness (13.2:1 on the card) and every tyre mark carries its letter S, M or H
validation.subject: our cars are white #ffffff (car 27) and #b9bcc6 (car 12), every other car #5f6270; a white mark always has a 2px card-colored gap around it
validation.sequential: one purple hue #5d3c94 → #d1befe (dim to bright, because on a dark card a larger value is brighter): monotone lightness, adjacent ΔL ≥ 0.06, dim end 2.19:1, hue spread 1°
validation.diverging: faster arm #6f4bac → #bb9ef9 and slower arm #7b5f06 → #d6ab32 each pass the ordinal checks (dim ends 2.83 and 3.01:1, hue spread ≤ 1°); midpoint #4a4d57
validation.text: label steps on the card: purple #c4b5fd 9.8:1, green #6ee7a8 11.8:1, yellow #f2c94c 11.4:1, red #ff8f87 8.2:1; #aaaaaa 7.8:1

code.note: the screen's own text steps (purple keyword, green string, yellow number, red function), all ≥ 4.5:1 on #0d0d14

sans.role: titles, sentences, notes and table names. Barlow stands in for the broadcast sans; the official Formula 1 typefaces and Titillium Web are not used

display.role: condensed capitals for labels, tiles and tabs (English only; Korean labels use Pretendard 600 without capitals) and every timing numeral: lap times, gaps, positions, car codes and the onboard display's digits stay Barlow Condensed in Korean too, with tabular figures

scale.headline: 31px/600 (ko 27px), line-height 1.22
scale.label: 13.5px/600 condensed capitals, letter-spacing .08em
scale.gear: 98px/700 Barlow Condensed, the P at half size and grey: the finishing position in the onboard display
scale.dial: 31px/700 Barlow Condensed in a 240° arc with a 9px stroke; scale ends 12.5px/600 #aaaaaa

rows: header 60px, one line: team and report in condensed capitals, round tabs (pill, the selected one white with black text), EN/KO

first screen, two columns (560px | 1fr): eyebrow (round · city · laps · date, FINAL CLASSIFICATION tag), the result in one or two sentences, the second car and points against plan, then the onboard display; Figure 1 circuit map on the right, the same height

onboard display: 15 shift lights (last 15 laps against the winner: green quicker, yellow slower, dark in- or out-lap), pit stop average dial (2.0–3.5 s, white target tick 2.50), finishing position as the gear readout with ▲ from grid, team points dial (0–43, white plan tick), two readouts below (gap to win, best lap with a purple chip when it is the race's fastest)

Figure 1 circuit map: the track as a dark band, 24 mini-sectors coloured by the best-lap gap to the winner on the diverging ramp, white S/F and sector lines, turn numbers outside, sector and lap gaps in the foot
01 Race: Figure 2 timing tower with tyre stints (1.15) · Figure 3 gap to the winner by lap (1), pit cycles shaded and dashed, tyre strips below
02 Lap: Figure 4 speed trace of both best laps and the running gap below (up = ahead, purple; down = behind, yellow), sector lines, turn numbers, a small circuit with the cursor position
03 Pit lane and season: Figure 5 pit stops · Figure 6 season points; Table 1 stint report (lap bar, average lap, wear bar, best lap chip, stop, note)
04 How it's built · 05 How the numbers are counted · footer

motion.grow: 0.5s, stints grow from the left, 120ms apart
motion.map: 0.3s fade per mini-sector, 28ms apart, in lap order

tableau.fonts: Tableau Book for text; Barlow and Barlow Condensed only if installed on every viewing machine and the server

measured.date: 2026-11-11, built-in browser, formula1.com/en/results/2026/races and the round pages (race result, qualifying, starting grid, pit stop summary, fastest laps)
measured.page: surfaces #000000, #15151e and #1c1c25; rules #303037 and #47464c; text #ffffff and #aaaaaa; table heads 14px/600 uppercase #aaaaaa, padding 16px 24px 16px 4px; cells 16px/600, 58px rows, 1px #303037 bottom rule; radii 8px, 50% and 1000px on site chrome
measured.notation: race time 1:35:23.504; gaps +14.602s; lapped +2 laps; lap times 1:12.689; DNF, DNS, NC; positions P1 in broadcasts
measured.not_used: logos, the Formula1 display face, Titillium Web, team colors and liveries, photos, real teams, drivers, circuits and results

notice.why: Formula 1's guidelines ask for this exact sentence and do not allow F1 marks in product names, so the style takes the name of the format (Race Timing) and says what it was read from only here
